sourceInformation.perspective: First person on a scripted rail camera (Mode 7 depth view), free crosshair
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 full engine (Mode 7, Arcade, Shell modules; 5 small engine edits), AI Hub session client 1.4.0, plain JavaScript in one HTML file; Node 24 and Playwright 1.63.0 for tests and the bundle
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native PS1/SNES pixel style: shaded HD Humanoid rigs, shapes-as-data vehicles and props, painted Mode 7 floors and Backdrop skies, pixel-art HUD and screens
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's rig system (walk/run from velocity, point and aim, throw move, kneel, crouch, die, down, expressions, portraits) plus custom solvePose poses: hands up, bound hands, panic, officer's whistle, rocket on the shoulder, parachute; rotors, wheels, toppling masts, collapsing tower as code
sourceInformation.audio: All synthesized in code with the engine's chip synth: about 50 sound effects, 13 original songs with intensity layers, Animalese-style gibberish voices per speaker through a per-letter Dialog hook, the wolf howl, stereo-panned by screen position, storm wind gusts
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared-world co-op for 1-4 players (host sim, client mirror, own card); local co-op for 1-4 with drop-in controllers
sourceInformation.testing: Headless node:vm suites driven by game.advance and the bot (one command, failures plus a count), a whole-game bot playthrough, Playwright browser checks of the final file, the real AI Hub harness; screenshots for look only
sourceInformation.research: Planner: Wikipedia and arcade-history.com on Operation Wolf; builder: none beyond the engine's and the hub's docs; title: the builder brainstormed 50 riffs and drew #10 with python secrets.randbelow
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown
sourceInformation.usage: Cost and tokens: unknown. Session time: about 1 hour 17 minutes (18:43:37 to 20:00)

testingFeedback: About 18 issues were caught by the headless suites, the bot playthroughs and the browser checks.

6 were critical: enemy types overwritten by same-named projectile types (knife throwers and mortar crews), enemies never attacking because a stun timer started undefined, an endless reload loop with part-used magazines, the final gunship flying above the screen, a boss part hidden behind its own hull, and continues that replayed the same lost fight forever.
The headless bot playthrough of each operation that reported damage taken by source.
Screenshots of static menus: they found nothing a script had not.
engineFeedback: Mode 7 with project and toFloor: the same math draws the world and hit-tests the shots.
Yes: rig heights in world units are not documented, so I measured them in a browser; E.store silently forgets everything where storage is blocked.
The light-gun loop: screen-space hit shapes, the rail camera with holds, telegraphs and the bot.
Mode 7 draws as an overlay, so the engine's lights and particles do not apply; FX and the night mask had to be my own.

A function voice for Dialog (per letter), a settings-rows screen and hidden groups for Shell, PlayStation glyphs by default, E.store keeping data for the visit when storage is blocked, and stereo pan for sound effects.
A first-person gallery mode for Mode 7 that keeps lighting, particles and hit picking.
promptFeedback: A clear deliverable plus a detailed plan to build from.
The plan's names (max effort, 17:47:46) differ from the task's names; the task wins, but it costs a moment.
The content volume: six operations, six bosses, cutscenes, co-op and netcode in one session.
Let the plan carry the exact deliverable names, or state that the names always come from TASK.md.

aiHub.name: Operation Big Bad Wolf
aiHub.tagline: Every bullet counts. Bring them home.
aiHub.description: A first-person light-gun rail shooter for 1-4 players: storm the Brimstone Coast with limited ammo, spare the civilians and rescue five hostages from the Hyena Legion.
aiHub.controls: Mouse or stick aims · click/R2 fires · right click/L2 grenade · R/□ reload
